gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the base Model Y trims (formerly 'Standard', now just RWD/AWD) skip the factory 8-inch rear screen and cost $7,000 less than the Premium AWD, or that a third-party 8.66-inch Android rear screen sells for $359 (Hansshow H86, fits Model Y 2020–2025.02) and a clip-in Model Y projector screen plus projector costs $379.98 (Aurzen AutoCinema $119.99 + ZIP $259.99).
standout_why: I checked the cited tesla.com pages (/modely, /learn/introducing-new-model-y, the owner's-manual Touchscreen page) and they returned HTTP 403, so I couldn't read them. The manual's rear-touchscreen text, which I read on ManualsLib (result #16, the same manual), lists features: two Bluetooth headphones, climate, seat heat, video, games, and locking the rear display from the front. It gives no trim fitment and no prices. Notateslaapp (#18) gives base prices of $39,990 RWD and $41,990 AWD but says nothing about a rear screen. ChatGPT's answer says only that 'some Standard versions do not' have the screen. It gives no price gap and names no aftermarket option.
decides: If you want a rear screen in a new Model Y, the answer is the Premium trim: the base AWD is $7,000 cheaper but has no rear display (cars.com). Aftermarket screens priced today ($359 Hansshow H86) are made for 2020–2025.02 cars, so they're the pick for older Model Ys and not a cheap fix for a new base car. A projector screen works in any Model Y but needs a separate projector, so the real cost is $379.98 or more.
